review_notes: Read every one of the 182 actual Luke 4–7 source units, all 175 retained source/target/rationale comparisons and all 10 deferral reasons against the exact original cache, with relevant surrounding target and source context.

All target IDs resolve, target ranges are contiguous in original order, pair keys are unique, no target contains its own source unit, and the paired/deferred sets exactly cover all 182 source units without overlap. The three additional pairs cover separate clauses or an explicit prophetic/Gospel counterpart rather than extra source credit.

Temptation ordering, stone versus stones, and Luke's shorter bread-only answer are retained. Deuteronomy's fear/serve wording is distinguished from worship/exclusive-service wording rather than silently harmonized. Psalms 90:11–12 is the actual canonical numbering and retains its fuller guarding phrase.

Isaiah 61's healing-the-brokenhearted clause and Luke's additional release-of-the-oppressed clause are correctly distinguished, with Isaiah58:6 supplying the latter's bounded comparison. Luke's acceptable-year reading stops before Isaiah's recompense and consolation continuation. The introduction and fulfillment links do not claim that Isaiah narrates the scroll-handling scene.

Hometown synagogue similarities and the later Capernaum parallels do not create a merged visit chronology. Luke4:44 actually says Judea while Mark1:39 says Galilee; the proposal explicitly preserves this geographical difference.

Boat-teaching and fishing comparisons distinguish the occasions and instructions. Luke's nets begin to tear and its boats begin to sink; John's resurrection catch is a separate event and John21:11 explicitly says its net was not torn. Unstated boat-partner details remain deferred.
Levi is not assigned another tax collector's identity. The apostle-list comparisons preserve sequence, Simon's epithets and Judas of James without equating that Judas with a different named apostle.

Blessings and woes distinguish poverty from poor-in-spirit, hunger from hunger-for-righteousness, laughter from consolation, and present/future reversal from Isaiah65's contrasted groups. Jeremiah5:31's actual people-loving-unjust-prophecy wording supports the limited acclaim comparison.

Related sermon sayings preserve reciprocity versus greeting, lending versus accepting borrowers, mercy versus perfection, release wording, measure's hearing/giving contexts, cloak/tunic order and lawsuit details, as well as rock/deep-foundation versus sand/no-foundation imagery.

The centurion scene retains elders and friends in Luke and the direct appeal in Matthew. Its internal worthy/unworthy contrast compares different speakers rather than declaring Jesus contradictory. No independent synagogue-benefactor identity is invented.

The Nain raising is compared with the widow's son in Kings and other raising commands only within their stated motifs. Mother/child, bier/hand, funeral location and different reported regions remain distinct. Unique Nain travel details are deferred.

John's inquiry and Jesus' sign list have precise Matthean parallels. The Malachi3:1 comparison preserves look-to-a-way, My face and the additional sanctuary/covenant-messenger language rather than replacing it with the Gospel's Thy face wording.

The anointing comparisons preserve the unnamed woman in Luke, Mary in John, Simon the Pharisee versus Simon the leper, head versus feet, tears versus perfume and different meal accounts. No women or their histories are identified. The prophet-knowledge comparison is a contrast with John's Samaritan woman, not a shared biography.

Internal debt/love interpretation links state the text's own comparisons while retaining because she loved much and avoiding an added earned-forgiveness theory. Distinct pronouncements of forgiveness and faith/peace formulae are not made into identical recipients or events.

All 10 deferred outcomes conservatively retain their specific unresolved scene details with zero credit. This peer review supports the retained English passage comparisons within their expressed limits, not exhaustive concordance, critical-text verification or independent historical confirmation.
